verdict.probe_answer: Arm A tests would fail on pre-change code, at minimum because the old 2-arg signature and bool return do not match. Strongest test: commit_precedence_and_comment_only_falls_back_to_title, because it checks typed/file/title precedence, comment-only fallback, CommitSource values, and adds an oversize candidate edge. Weakest test: the derived bounding check still only asserts prefix/length rather than the exact truncated subject. Arm B tests would also fail on pre-change code for the same signature/enum reasons. Strongest test: commit_precedence_and_comment_only_falls_back_to_title covers the main precedence and comment-only title fallback. Weakest test: that new test asserts only .0, so source/warning regressions for Typed/Title could pass; it also lacks Arm A's oversize candidate edge.
verdict.rationale: Both arms implement the required call-site ripple in main.rs and merge.rs and keep scope limited to the requested files. SMELL (Arm B): commit_candidate bounds after NUL/comment stripping, so a raw candidate over 64 KiB hidden inside comments can still be accepted; the brief's read_commit_msg_file mirror points more toward Arm A's raw candidate bound. SMELL (Arm B tests): source values are only partly tested, so the Derived-warning contract is less protected. SMELL (Arm A): it adapts CommitSource back to a bool for decide instead of fully carrying the enum through that internal tuple, but the required warning and resolved message behavior are still preserved. Arm A is materially better because its tests are stricter and it is closer to the stated bounding model.
